Experienced meditator here.

Silence is preferable for beginners, but is definitely not a must. In fact, the desired goal of meditation practice, is to be able to find a calm mental state in the most hectic situations.

The Soto Zen school in Japan encourages students to face a wall. Yoga, obviously encourages meditation while exercising. Ascetic christians often use chants, such repeating the extremely short "Jesus Prayer".

Based on my experiences, I'd recommend being as still as possible, don't even scratch an itch if you can bear it. Allow yourself to breathe, to blink, and even to think, but not to do anything else (including looking around and including do not listen to music).

My very favorite is the "standing meditation" (being on your feet), while outdoors. Since your butt doesn't fall asleep you may find that for sessions longer than about 10 minutes, it's actually MORE comfortable than seated meditation.

Try starting with 5 minutes a day, and add one minute per day until you're up to 30 minutes. Then add a second session of 5 minutes, until you work your way up to one 30 and one 20 minute sessions.

Remind yourself constantly of the rock solid, proven benefits of meditation- you'll require less sleep. Redude blood pressure. Live longer. Increase testosterone. Increase pain tolerance. Etc.

Considering that it's free, and can be done anywhere, meditation is pretty much all upsides and no downsides. The only people who should avoid meditating are schizophrenics, or anyone who hears voices in their head. So hopefully, not you.

Above all, remember that the more you "don't have time" to meditate, and the more you "don't feel like it", the more you probably need to.
